summary: OAuthFlow class implementing OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code grant with optional PKCE. Handles authorize URL building, code exchange, token refresh, and expiry checking.

key_classes.name: OAuthFlow
key_classes.summary: Runs OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow. Takes a spec object with metadata containing authorize_url, token_url, optional use_pkce, default_scope, callback_port. Supports local_server and manual redirect modes.

key_functions.name: OAuthFlow.build_authorize_url
key_functions.summary: Returns (url, state) tuple. Adds PKCE code_challenge if use_pkce=True in metadata.

key_functions.name: OAuthFlow.exchange_code
key_functions.summary: POST to token_url with auth code. Returns flat dict with access_token, refresh_token, token_expires_at, scope.

key_functions.name: OAuthFlow.refresh
key_functions.summary: POST to token_url with refresh_token grant. Returns flat dict with new access_token and updated refresh_token.

key_functions.name: OAuthFlow.is_expired
key_functions.summary: Static method. Returns True if token_expires_at is within buffer_seconds (default 300s) of now.

key_functions.name: OAuthFlow.authorize
key_functions.summary: Full end-to-end flow: build URL, open browser or prompt, wait for callback, exchange code.

lifecycle_notes: PKCE code_verifier is stored as instance state (_code_verifier), tied to a single authorize/exchange cycle
documentation_hooks: Flow diagram: build_authorize_url -> browser -> callback -> exchange_code
risks: CSRF: state comparison is only checked in authorize(), not in exchange_code() directly

evidence.detail: Tests for build_authorize_url, exchange_code, refresh, is_expired
